items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: I think Dick already asked you this.

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I worked with Randy a long time, often and long. Mm-hmm. I worked with Chris Kelly. I worked with Buddy Petit. I worked with Jack Carey. I worked with Leslie Mayne. I worked with a fella called Big, One-Eyed Big, bass player. Mm-hmm. I worked with him. Oh, I worked with several bands around there, different places they'd go play in there. They'd sit on me there and have nothing but tones. I was in Idol, I stayed busy all the time.

What year did you say that was when you got into New Orleans? I went to New Orleans. I mean, when I got into New Orleans in 1980. Uh-huh. Yeah. But, trying to get some kind of picture of the style of clarinet you were playing then, I think Dick already asked you this. What you're playing now, the clarinet you're playing now, wasn't too much like what you were playing then? No. How was it different then?

Well, I was carrying the lead, moving on, doing more variation. I know the horn better then than I do now. See, I'm afraid to try to do anything with the horn of them, because I didn't forget to finger them or anything.
